### Observed differences

- In the earlier window, the elapsed time between the completion of A25 and the completion of A32 averaged about 0.87 hours (median about 0.89 h; the middle half of gaps fell between about 0.83 and 0.92 h), observed in 23 gaps — roughly 12 in 100 traces. In the later window, the same gap averaged about 0.42 hours (median about 0.42 h; middle half about 0.39–0.46 h), observed in 30 gaps — about 15 in 100 traces. That is a reduction of about 0.45 hours, roughly half the earlier duration. [TWAIT001]
- The two gap distributions barely overlap: even the slowest quarter of later-window gaps (up to about 0.46 h) lies well below the fastest quarter of earlier-window gaps (from about 0.83 h), and the spread narrowed (standard deviation from about 0.10 h to about 0.06 h). The slight rise in how often the gap is observed (about 12 to about 15 in 100 traces) is small enough to be consistent with sampling variation. [TWAIT001]
- No control-flow, ordering or participation differences reached the configured thresholds; this timing gap was the only qualifying item (screening expected about 0.3 control-flow items and about 0.02 time items by chance in an unchanged process). [TWAIT001]

### Inference

Support level: Supported hypothesis

The evidence supports a change in timing as a possibility: the elapsed time from the completion of A25 to the completion of A32 shortened by about 0.45 hours per occurrence, from roughly 0.87 hours in the earlier window to roughly 0.42 hours in the later one. Supporting signs: the shift is coherent across the entire distribution (all quartiles dropped by about 0.43–0.47 hours and the variability narrowed), the difference exceeds that seen in 1,999 of 2,000 random re-splits of the pooled data, and one qualifying time item against a chance expectation of about 0.02 in its family is many times what an unchanged process typically produces, while the control-flow family produced no items (about 0.3 expected), consistent with an unchanged structure. Limitations: the gap is observed in only about 12–15 in 100 traces, so the change is established for this activity pair rather than the process as a whole, and elapsed time between consecutive completions cannot separate shorter waiting from faster handling or fewer intervening completions. A competing explanation the evidence cannot rule out is a subtle sequencing change around A25 and A32 that fell below the control-flow screening thresholds and would shorten the measured gap without a pure timing change. [TWAIT001]

Other differences: none; the timing gap above was the only item to qualify at the configured thresholds. [TWAIT001]
